Without the .default + __esModule belt, TS under verbatimModuleSyntax:true rejects the default import; without `module.exports = preset` Tailwind's loader can't see the theme. The .d.cts file uses `export default preset` (NOT `export = preset`) because `import = require(...)` is disallowed under module:ESNext.

- **Prettier lowercases CSS hex but not JS hex.** After format:write, packages/ui/src/global.css has lowercase hex (#06140e) while tokens.ts and tailwind-preset.cjs keep uppercase (#06140E). CSS is case-insensitive for hex so this is semantically equivalent and the verify-no-hex-literals regex matches both cases. design-language.md keeps uppercase; tokens.ts MUST keep uppercase to match the AC's literal-equals assertion (the snapshot test pins this). If a future story tightens CSS hex case, it's a `.prettierrc` override, not a code change.

The pattern is `expect(tokens).toMatchSnapshot();` plus a non-hex structural assertion like Object.keys equality.

- **verify-no-hex-literals scoping.** Script scans `packages/` and `apps/` only — NOT `docs/` (where design-language.md lives) and NOT `scripts/` (where the script itself lives). The allow-list is by basename match (tokens.ts, global.css, tailwind-preset.cjs, tailwind-preset.d.cts, design-language.md, PRD.md) plus suffix match (.snap). Future stories that legitimately need hex in a NEW file (e.g. a colour-picker showcase) should add an explicit entry rather than disabling the script — keeps the perimeter tight.

- **Detecting prior-iteration scaffolds before pivoting.** First read of prd.json showed US-022 at priority 22; mid-iteration the owner inserted US-043 at priority 22 and bumped US-022 to 23 with new dependent ACs. The clue was the new docs/design-language.md untracked file plus the CLAUDE.md diff adding the UI Verification Protocol. - **Tailwind preset values are mirrored, not imported.** tokens.ts is ESM/TS; tailwind-preset.cjs is CJS/JS — Node CJS can't `require()` a .ts file at runtime without a loader. The duplication is intentional and allow-listed by the verify check. Snapshot test pins tokens.ts; future drift in either file is caught by the snapshot or by visual review. If a third source (e.g. a colour-picker UI) needs tokens, add a TS module that re-exports from tokens.ts; do NOT add a parallel source of values.

- **package.json exports map.** @signal-console/ui exposes `.` (index.ts), `./tokens`, `./tailwind-preset` (the .cjs file directly), `./global.css`, `./utilities.css`. The CSS exports are static asset paths that Vite/PostCSS consumers will resolve at build time; the .cjs export is what Tailwind's loader picks up via `presets: [require("@signal-console/ui/tailwind-preset")]`.
